key_insight: A single Mach- and height-conditioned diffusion model can reconstruct hypersonic near-wall turbulence from sparse top-wall data by stitching overlapping wall-normal subdomains and preserving spectral content.
engineering_relevance: This offers a probabilistic surrogate for hypersonic boundary-layer sensing and reconstruction, with potential use in reduced-observation diagnostics, uncertainty-aware modeling, and wall-adjacent flow prediction.
method: Train one conditional EDM jointly on M=6, 7, and 8 DNS data
Reconstruct overlapping wall-normal subdomains and merge them with soft inpainting for continuity
Add bounded binned spectral power loss to retain high-wavenumber structure during diffusion sampling
evidence_signal: Against DNS, the model reproduces instantaneous fields, spectra, statistics, correlations, wall quantities, and Trettel-Larsson-collapsed profiles across the training Mach numbers.
watch_item: The approach depends on good top-wall conditioning and subdomain blending, so extrapolation to unseen Mach numbers or stronger flow regimes may need retraining or careful validation.
paper_title: Multiscale Hypersonic Boundary Layer Reconstruction via Spectral Binning and Subdomain-wise Conditional Diffusion
